rows.note: This is the all-purpose Cantonese noun for a stage musical or musical film.

example.english: We watched a musical last night, and the songs and dancing were great.
example.traditional: 我哋噚晚睇咗套音樂劇，啲歌同舞都好精彩。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 cam4 maan5 tai2 zo2 tou3 jam1 ngok6 kek6 di1 go1 tung4 mou5 dou1 hou2 zing1 coi2

rows.jyutping: tung4 jam1 ngok6 jau5 gwaan1 ge3
rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose way to describe something that concerns music, including its performance or notation.

example.english: This book is about musical matters.
example.traditional: 呢本書講同音樂有關嘅嘢。
example.jyutping: ni1 bun2 syu1 gong2 tung4 jam1 ngok6 jau5 gwaan1 ge3 je5

rows.note: Use this for a voice, sound, or melody that is pleasing to hear.

example.jyutping: nei5 coeng3 ni1 sau2 go1 zan1 hai6 hou2 teng1

rows.note: Use this for someone who has musicality, a good ear, or natural musical ability rather than merely liking music.

example.english: They are very musical when they play the piano.
example.jyutping: keoi5 taan4 kam4 hou2 jau5 jam1 ngok6 gam2

rows.jyutping: hou2 zung1 ji3 jam1 ngok6 ge3 N
rows.note: Use this attributive construction when musical means fond of music, as in “a person who really likes music.”

example.english: My son is a musical person.
example.traditional: 我個仔係個好鍾意音樂嘅人。
example.jyutping: ngo5 go3 zai2 hai6 go3 hou2 zung1 ji3 jam1 ngok6 ge3 jan4
